newsitem.title: POLAND: EX-DEPUTY TREASURY MIN BECOMES PBI VICE-PRESIDENT.
newsitem.headline: EX-DEPUTY TREASURY MIN BECOMES PBI VICE-PRESIDENT.

text.p: Polish former deputy treasury minister Leszek Juchniewicz, who stepped down on March 1, became deputy president of the soon-to-be-privatised Polish Investment Bank (PBI), PBI spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

Anna Rybaltowska said in a statement PBI's board appointed Juchniewicz deputy president already on January 23, effective from the date when his resignation from the ministerial post is accepted by the prime minister.

Juchniewicz, who supervised the dragging privatisation of the country's largest newsstand chain Ruch, on Monday denied speculation that his removal from office last week was linked to the controversial privatisation deal.
The privatisation of Ruch has sparked controversy as a bid from a Polish-French consortium led by France's Hachette Distribution Services has been challenged by a late offer by a Polish group.
The ministry signed an initial agreement with Hachette on Ruch's sale in December 1996 but Juchniewicz later said the ministry would consider another bid if it proved competitive.
A rival bid was filed by a consortium led by trading company Universal last week.
